Q361.L1t: Einstein, Newton and Galileo are among the most celebrated scientists in history, and each made major discoveries.
Q361.L2t: The passage says these scientists invented many things for humankind and did thousands of experiments.
Q361.L3t: The passage says they did not get everything from school, that knowing how to study by oneself matters most, and that they worked hard all their lives, wasting no moment.
Q361.L4t: They succeeded because they knew how to study on their own and worked hard.
Q361.L2f: The passage says Einstein, Newton and Galileo mostly avoided experiments and relied on memorizing formulas.
Q361.L3f: The passage says the great scientists succeeded chiefly because they stayed in school longer than others and learned everything they needed from their teachers.
Q361.L4f: They succeeded mainly because they had received more schooling than other people.

Q790.L1t: The United States has a very large number of cars, which are widely used for business and for daily life.
Q790.L2t: The passage says some families have two or more cars, and cars are used for business and for driving children to school.
Q790.L3t: The passage says there are still many families without cars, while some families have two or more.
Q790.L4t: Cars are everywhere in America, but not every family owns one.
Q790.L2f: The passage says car pools were invented to let families sell their cars and save money on gas.
Q790.L3f: The passage says every household in the country owns at least one car, and the only difference is that some own more than one.
Q790.L4f: The United States is full of cars and every family has one.

Q379.L1t: The passage introduces several art districts in Chinese cities, each converted from former industrial or military buildings.
Q379.L2t: Tank Loft is described as a 12,000-square-meter art center, the largest contemporary art base in western China.
Q379.L3t: Tank Loft is on the campus of the Sichuan Fine Arts Institute, while the other three zones are on the grounds of old factories.
Q379.L4t: It differs from the others in where it is located, since it sits on a school campus rather than a former factory.
Q379.L2f: The passage says Tank Loft was established in 1956 and is open every day of the week.
Q379.L3f: The passage says Tank Loft is the only art zone with no galleries or studios and only an exhibition of military tanks, unlike the others.
Q379.L4f: It differs from the others in its feature, since its style is unlike any of the other art zones.
